facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is usable and shows improving credit metrics, with limits that the committee should hold alongside the ratios. facts.label: EBITDA definitions and add-back review
facts.text: - No source reports EBITDA or a covenant EBITDA; a search of all seven sources for EBITDA found no hit. Both EBITDA measures here are analyst constructs. The company's own measure is adjusted operating income, which is defined as GAAP operating income excluding amortization of intangible assets, net realized capital gains or losses and other items that neither relate to the ordinary course of business nor reflect underlying performance (Q3 10-Q page:35). - Reported EBITDA is GAAP operating income plus depreciation and amortization from the cash flow statement. It carries every one-off through the period. In FY2025 it is depressed by the goodwill impairment of 5,725 recorded in Q3 2025. - Adjusted EBITDA is adjusted operating income plus depreciation and amortization less amortization of intangible assets, because adjusted operating income already adds back that amortization and adding the whole of D&A would count it twice. The check is that adjusted EBITDA less reported EBITDA equals the add-backs other than amortization of intangibles: 7,807 for FY2025 and 256 for LTM Q3 2026. - FY2025 add-backs other than amortization (10-K page:138): net realized capital losses 44, acquisition-related integration costs 117, goodwill impairment 5,725, Health Care Delivery clinic closure 83, opioid litigation charge 320, office real estate 10, legacy litigation charges 1,220 and loss on Accountable Care assets 288. The litigation items are cash claims, so adjusted EBITDA overstates cash earnings available for debt service in the periods they are paid. - LTM Q3 2026 add-backs other than amortization of 256 comprise the Omnicare guarantee of 193 and 63 of realized capital losses and integration costs; the 2025 items have rolled out of the window. - Net investment income of 2,456 on an LTM basis (FY2025 2,233 plus nine months 2026 1,862 less nine months 2025 1,639) is part of revenue and operating income, so EBITDA includes insurance investment income. - Departures from a covenant definition cannot be assessed because none is disclosed. The only covenant statements are that the facilities and unsecured senior notes contain customary restrictive financial and operating covenants, that they do not accelerate on a downgrade, and that the Company was in compliance at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:64).

facts.label: Segment drivers
facts.text: Health Care Benefits drives the change: its adjusted operating income was 6,379 for nine months 2026 against 3,615, and the medical benefit ratio was 91.3 percent in Q3 2026 against 92.8 percent and 87.8 percent against 90.0 percent for nine months (Q3 release page:2), which the Q3 10-Q (page:54) attributes to improved underlying performance in the Government business. Health Services rose by 100 and Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness by 178 over the nine months, while Corporate/Other was 387 worse. Implied Q4 2025 adjusted operating income for Health Care Benefits is a loss of 676 (2,939 less 3,615), so the LTM window replaces that weak quarter and part of the LTM improvement over FY2025 is a base effect. Underwriting results in one segment are therefore the swing factor for the EBITDA denominator.

facts.label: Cash flow quality
facts.text: - Nine months 2026 operating cash flow was 15,318 against 7,249. The Q3 10-Q (page:63) says the increase was primarily due to the timing of receipts and payments and improved operating performance in Health Care Benefits. Accounts receivable used 2,254 against 7,537 a year earlier and other liabilities provided 2,810 (page:4), so working capital swung. Full-year 2026 guidance is cash flow from operations of at least 15.5 billion (Q3 release page:1). - LTM operating cash flow of 18,708 is below LTM adjusted EBITDA of 19,837; LTM free cash flow of 15,567 less dividends of 3,423 leaves 12,144. In nine months 2026 the Company repaid 4,057 of long-term debt, issued none, and cash rose from 8,453 to 11,738. No share repurchases appear in the nine months 2026 or 2025 cash flow statements. - LTM interest paid has stayed between 2,991 and 3,070 across the four dates, so the cover improvement comes from the numerator, not from lower interest.

facts.label: Liquidity by facility
facts.text: - Three unsecured five-year back-up revolving credit facilities of 2,500 each (7,500 in total), all undrawn at September 30, 2026, with no commercial paper outstanding; expiries May 2029, 2030 and 2031; weighted average quarterly facility fee about 0.03 percent (Q3 10-Q page:64). None expires within twelve months. - Letters of credit drawn on the facilities: Not supplied. Searches for letter of credit, standby, LC and LCs across the 10-K and the Q3 10-Q found nothing, so net availability equals the face amount only on the assumption of no usage, which the sources neither confirm nor deny. - Consolidated liquidity is 11,738 plus 7,500, which is 19,238. Parent and nonrestricted liquidity is about 5,900 plus 7,500, which is 13,400, because the rest of the cash sits in regulated or restricted subsidiaries. Restricted cash of 210 (in other assets) is excluded. FHLBB advances of up to about 1,400 are available to a subsidiary but are not committed facilities and are excluded. - Near-term uses: current portion of long-term debt of 3,457, and the current portion of opioid settlement obligations, which was 648 at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:155); the 2026 equivalent is Not supplied. - Between the March and June 2026 10-Qs the facility expiries moved from May 2028, 2029, 2030 to May 2029, 2030, 2031, with no amendment document in the pack. The later dates are used and labelled as filing wording.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: CVS Health is a diversified, listed health care company with four reportable segments: Health Care Benefits (the Aetna insurer), Health Services (the CVS Caremark pharmacy benefit manager plus clinical and care delivery businesses including Signify Health and Oak Street Health), Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness (the retail and infusion pharmacy business) and Corporate/Other. For a creditor the mechanics are: a very large, low-margin revenue base dominated by drug pass-through; an insurance segment whose results swing on the medical benefit ratio and on government rate and risk-adjustment policy; a pharmacy segment under reimbursement and price pressure; and a group that carries a large debt stack with unsecured senior notes and two junior subordinated series. The recent history that matters is a reset in 2025 (a goodwill impairment in the care delivery business, exits from accountable care programs, an individual exchange premium deficiency and the Omnicare bankruptcy) followed by a stronger 2026 in which Health Care Benefits recovered and the group repaid debt while leaving the dividend unchanged. The leading uncertainty is the announced separation: it is a proposed transaction, not a completed one, and nothing in the pack says how existing notes, facilities, guarantees or the junior subordinated notes would be allocated. There is no sponsor, no leveraged buyout and no sponsor behaviour to assess, so the governance review rests on documented issuer actions only, and ownership and control detail is Insufficient Information because the proxy statement is incorporated by reference and not supplied.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The only announced transaction is a proposed separation of CVS Health into two independent, publicly traded companies, announced on November 4, 2026 and disclosed as a subsequent event to the September 30, 2026 financial statements (Q3 10-Q page:40 and page:44). It is intended to be tax-free to the Company and its shareholders for U.S. federal income tax purposes. One company would hold Aetna, CVS Caremark, CVS Specialty, Oak Street Health and Signify Health and would carry the CVS Health name in the interim; the other would hold retail pharmacy, mail pharmacy, MinuteClinic including virtual care and the Health100 technology services business and would be named CVS Pharmacy. Completion is expected in the first half of 2028, subject to customary conditions including final approval by the Board, effectiveness of a Form 10 registration statement and a customary confirmation of tax-free treatment. This is a labelled future date, not a fact. The pack gives no purchase price, use of proceeds, new debt, debt allocation, guarantee, change-of-control or covenant treatment for the separation, so its liquidity and leverage effect is Insufficient Information. The creditor mechanic is that two entities will replace one obligor and the existing indentures and facilities will have to be dealt with; whether that is by assumption, guarantee, exchange or retained parent obligations is unknown, and that is the main monitoring item.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: On new debt issues, no debt was issued in nine months 2026 (the cash flow statement shows no proceeds from long-term debt and repayments of long-term debt, Q3 10-Q page:4). Earlier issuance in the notes: on May 9, 2024 senior notes of about 5.0 billion dollars in five series for general corporate purposes; on December 10, 2024 two junior subordinated series of 2.25 billion and 750 million dollars with fixed-to-fixed rate resets, whose proceeds funded a cash tender in which about 2.6 billion dollars of senior notes were bought for about 2.0 billion dollars in cash with a gain on early extinguishment of 491 million dollars; and on August 15, 2025 senior notes in four series of 750 million, 1.5 billion, 1.25 billion and 500 million dollars due 2032, 2035, 2055 and 2065 with total proceeds of about 4.0 billion dollars used to repay existing indebtedness including commercial paper and for general corporate purposes (10-K page:151 to page:152). The creditor reading is that the Company has used long-dated issuance and a liability management tender to extend and reshape the stack, and has since moved to repayment. Other transactions relevant to credit are the Omnicare matters and the Rite Aid asset acquisitions below.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: Health Care Benefits revenue from the federal government is approximately 20 percent of consolidated revenues, and Medicare contracts with CMS are the large majority of it (10-K page:11); Medicare Advantage membership was 4,229 thousand at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:55). Mechanic: government contracts are annual and subject to rate notices and risk adjustment, so revenue is visible but earnings depend on policy. Implication: revenue durability is good but margin resilience depends on government rates and medical cost trend, so leverage tolerance should be tested for a reversal in the Government business medical benefit ratio. No logged conflict counters this. 2. Margin and cash flow risk. Evidence: the medical benefit ratio was 87.8 percent for nine months 2026 against 90.0 percent, with lower favorable prior period development (Q3 10-Q page:55), and Health Care Benefits adjusted operating income rose strongly (financial base handoff). Mechanic: small changes in the ratio on a premium base of this size move group earnings. Implication: the improvement in leverage reported in the financial base handoff rests on one segment and is not yet a through-the-cycle measure; monitoring should centre on medical cost trend and prior period development. 3. Concentration risk. Evidence: no single Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness payor is 10 percent or more of revenue (10-K page:29), while Health Services revenue growth is driven by drug mix and brand inflation with client price improvements (Q3 10-Q page:58). Mechanic: PBM contracts reprice at renewal and legislation targets PBM activities (Q3 10-Q page:48). Implication: the largest client terms are not disclosed, so concentration inside the PBM cannot be judged. 4. Sponsor alignment. There is no sponsor; ownership alignment cannot be assessed beyond the dividend and repurchase record. Implication: no sponsor extraction or support risk applies; public shareholder distributions are modest and documented. 5. Key uncertainties. Evidence: separation announced for completion in the first half of 2028 (Q3 10-Q page:40); opioid accrual of about 3.4 billion dollars remaining (Q3 10-Q page:28); Omnicare guarantee (page:39). Mechanic: each is a claim or a structural change that the debt figure does not capture. Implication: refinancing and guarantor analysis should wait for the Form 10 and any indenture amendments; the committee should not assume that existing creditors keep their current obligor.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: CVS Health Corporation is an improving, moderate-leverage credit whose 2026 progress rests heavily on one segment. The strongest support is deleveraging: total debt to adjusted EBITDA fell to 3.06x on LTM Q3 2026 from 3.78x at FY2025, adjusted EBITDA to cash interest rose to 6.51x, and undrawn back-up facilities of USD 7,500 million sit beside cash of USD 11,738 million. The weakest point is that Health Care Benefits supplied more than the whole net rise in adjusted operating income, while covenant levels, guarantor terms and the debt allocation under the announced separation are not disclosed. What decides the outcome is whether the medical benefit ratio holds, and what the separation does to the obligor and guarantee structure before completion, expected in the first half of 2028.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, leverage and cover have improved on both numerator and denominator. Total debt carrying value fell from USD 64,570 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 60,680 million at September 30, 2026 while LTM adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 17,073 million to USD 19,837 million, taking total debt to adjusted EBITDA from 3.78x to 3.06x and net debt to adjusted EBITDA from 3.29x to 2.47x [CP-1]. The mechanic is repayment of USD 4,057 million of long-term debt with no issuance in nine months 2026 and higher earnings, so debt service is better covered. The implication is lower refinancing and leverage risk, but the EBITDA is our construct because the company reports none and discloses no covenant definition.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Second, the earnings recovery is concentrated. Adjusted operating income by segment moved from USD 14,443 million at FY2025 to USD 17,098 million on LTM Q3 2026; Health Care Benefits rose by USD 2,764 million while Health Services rose by USD 100 million, Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness by USD 178 million and Corporate/Other fell by USD 387 million (Calculations). Health Care Benefits recorded an implied loss of USD 676 million in Q4 2025 [CP-1], so the LTM window replaces a weak quarter, and its medical benefit ratio of 87.8 percent for nine months 2026 against 90.0 percent reflects the absence of 2025 premium deficiency reserves and lower favorable prior period development [CP-1A]. The mechanic is underwriting leverage on a large premium base; the implication is that a reversal would raise leverage quickly (see the sensitivity below).

facts.text: Third, liquidity is adequate but less deep than the consolidated cash suggests. Consolidated cash of USD 11,738 million includes about USD 5,900 million held by the parent or nonrestricted subsidiaries, plus USD 7,500 million of undrawn facilities that now expire in May 2029, 2030 and 2031, and no commercial paper [CP-1]. Against that, the next twelve months include a current portion of long-term debt of USD 3,457 million, a dividend of about USD 3,423 million on an LTM basis and an opioid settlement obligation whose current portion was USD 648 million at December 31, 2025, together USD 7,528 million; parent-level liquidity of USD 13,400 million covers that 1.78x. The weak spots are that letters of credit on the facilities are not supplied and that nine months 2026 operating cash flow of USD 15,318 million was helped by working-capital timing.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. The group has scale and diversification across insurance, pharmacy benefits and retail pharmacy, with USD 420,614 million of LTM revenue and adjusted operating income positive in three of four segments [CP-1]. Deleveraging has been funded from internal cash flow, with USD 12,144 million of LTM free cash flow after dividends, no 2026 issuance and no share repurchases in nine months 2026 [CP-1, CP-1A]. Liquidity is supported by USD 7,500 million of undrawn facilities with the earliest expiry in May 2029, so no facility matures within twelve months [CP-1]. The maturity profile is manageable in the near term, with USD 3,379 million due in 2027 and USD 5,008 million in 2028 per the schedule at December 31, 2025, against LTM free cash flow of USD 15,567 million and the facilities [CP-1]. Reporting is regular and discloses segment reconciliations and subsequent events [CP-1A].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Earnings are concentrated: Health Care Benefits drove the improvement and about 20 percent of consolidated revenue comes from the federal government, mainly Medicare contracts [CP-1A]. Protections cannot be assessed because covenant levels, guarantors and indentures are not supplied [CP-0, CP-1]. Cash is partly outside the parent, and letters of credit usage is unknown [CP-1]. The debt stack includes USD 3,000 million of junior subordinated notes in two series and unsecured senior notes, so structural and ranking questions arise on a separation [CP-1]. Claims outside debt are large: the opioid accrual, lease liabilities and the Omnicare guarantee [CP-1, CP-1A]. The separation introduces an unresolved change of obligor, and pharmacy segments face reimbursement and price pressure, with Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness revenue down 2.0 percent in Q3 2026 [CP-1A].

### Readiness view

Overall view: READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS. The effective source set is sufficient for the owners of CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 to perform their methods on a consolidated CVS Health Corporation perimeter. The strongest contrary evidence is that the debt documents are not in the pack: the 2026 filings carry debt only as totals, so facility-level and covenant analysis is bounded by the annual filing and by what the quarterly filings state. No source is blocked, no critical identity boundary is unresolved, and no consumer is CONDITIONAL. Missing downstream analytical handoffs are not counted against source readiness. Where a model objective is assessed, the assertion is SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED.

### Source-by-source assessment

- 10-K FY2025 (original authority: audited annual report filed with the SEC). Cover at page:1 names CVS HEALTH CORPORATION, Commission file number 001-01011, fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. Note 10 Borrowings and Credit Agreements at page:235 and page:236 holds the full debt table, five-year repayments, back-up facilities and the FHLBB capacity. Debt covenants and ratings at page:153. Contractual obligations including operating and finance leases and Target lease obligations at page:155 and page:156. Lease note at pages 229 to 230.
- 10-Q Q1 2026 (unaudited interim). Balance sheet and cash flow at page:3 and page:4; fair value of long-term debt at page:16; facilities and covenants at page:52 and page:53.
- 10-Q Q2 2026 (unaudited interim). Balance sheet at page:3; six-month cash flow at page:4; fair value of long-term debt at page:17 and page:18; facilities, covenants and ratings at page:59.

- 10-Q Q3 2026 (unaudited interim, the most recent filing and the primary source for the current period). Statement of operations at page:2; balance sheet at page:3 and page:14 for investments; cash flow at page:4; restricted cash at page:10; fair value of long-term debt at page:18; lease guarantees at page:23; segment note with reconciliations to operating income at page:35 to page:37; Omnicare guarantee footnote at page:39; Note 10 Subsequent Event at page:40; liquidity at page:63; commercial paper, back-up facilities, FHLBB, covenants and ratings at page:64; medical benefit ratio discussion at page:54.

- Earnings releases (Exhibit 99.1; management presentation, supporting attributed claims, not controlling over filings). Q3 release: headline results, guidance and cash flow from operations at page:1, statement of operations at page:6, cash flow at page:7, non-GAAP reconciliations at page:11 to page:13. Q1 and Q2 releases give headline results and guidance on page:1 and operating commentary on page:2. No investor presentation is in the pack; the releases take that place.

Extraction status is separate from fidelity. The extractions are flattened text of HTML filings; the tables read cleanly and tie out (see Calculations), but no image, chart or layout inspection is claimed and none was needed because the pack holds no deck or scan.
### Perimeter and roles

- The reporting entity in every filing is CVS Health Corporation, consolidated, in USD. The notes table does not name the issuer or co-issuer of each series, any guarantor, or security. The 10-K and 10-Q covenant paragraphs describe the back-up revolving credit facilities and unsecured senior notes as carrying customary restrictive financial and operating covenants (page:153; page:64). Issuer-by-series, guarantor and subsidiary-level debt detail are therefore Not supplied.

- Cash is not all at the parent: of approximately $11.7 billion cash and cash equivalents at September 30, 2026, approximately $5.9 billion was held by the parent company or nonrestricted subsidiaries (page:63 of the Q3 10-Q). Restricted cash of $210 million sits in other assets (page:10).

- The Omnicare entities were deconsolidated in September 2025 (page:40, footnote 14). For Q3 2026 the Company recorded an estimated contingent guarantee liability, labelled Omnicare guarantee, of $193 million (page:36; footnote 7 at page:39). The agreements themselves are not in the pack.

- Dated ratings are company statements, not agency documents: at September 30, 2026 long-term debt rated BBB by Fitch, Baa3 by Moody's and BBB by S&P; outlook Negative by Fitch and Stable by S&P; in August 2026 Moody's changed its outlook from Stable to Positive (page:64).
### Evidence coverage for the requested objective

- Discrete quarters and fiscal years: Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 income statements and balance sheets are present, with FY2025 from the 10-K. Q3 2025 and nine months 2025 comparatives are in the Q3 2026 10-Q (page:2). Q4 2025 is not a separate source; it would have to be derived as FY2025 less nine months 2025.

- Quarter versus year-to-date: the 10-Q cash flow statements are cumulative (three, six and nine months), so a discrete Q2 or Q3 cash flow needs subtraction of the earlier year-to-date figure. The releases do not remove that need.

- Segments and add-backs: four reportable segments, adjusted operating income by segment and a full reconciliation to GAAP operating income for three and nine months of both years (page:36 to page:37 of the Q3 10-Q). Depreciation and amortization is given by segment on the same pages.
- KPIs: medical benefit ratio discussion is at page:54 of the Q3 10-Q and page:17 of the Q3 release.
- Cash paid for interest and tax: nine months 2026 interest paid $2,586 million and income taxes paid $708 million (page:4 of the Q3 10-Q).

- Facility-level debt and carrying values: 49 senior note and junior subordinated note lines, finance leases and other at December 31, 2025 (page:235 to page:236 of the 10-K). At September 30, 2026 only totals: current portion of long-term debt $3,457 million and long-term debt $57,223 million (page:3), with fair value $54,977 million against carrying value $60,680 million (page:18).

- Liquidity: three $2.5 billion five-year unsecured back-up revolving credit facilities, no commercial paper and no borrowings under them at September 30, 2026; FHLBB capacity approximately $1.4 billion, no advances (page:64).
- Business and transaction narrative: separation announcement (page:40), operational updates and guidance in each release, litigation and contingencies in Note 8 (page:22 onward).
### Version relationships and conflicts
- The three quarterly filings and the 10-K are separate active sources for different dates; none supersedes another. No duplicate sources.

- Back-up facility expiry wording changes. The 10-K (page:236) and the Q1 10-Q (page:52) say the facilities expire in May 2028, 2029 and 2030. The Q2 10-Q (page:59) and Q3 10-Q (page:64) say May 2029, 2030 and 2031. The cause (extension, renewal or replacement) is not stated in any supplied source, and no credit agreement is supplied. Downstream effect: the later date must be used for runway, labelled as filing wording, with the amendment as a gap.

- Rating outlook sequence is not a conflict: the Q1 10-Q (page:53) shows Negative at both Fitch and S&P and Stable at Moody's; the Q2 10-Q (page:59) records S&P moved to Stable in May 2026; the Q3 10-Q (page:64) records Moody's moved to Positive in August 2026.
- No filing-versus-release conflict was found. Headline cash flow from operations in each release matches the filing (see Calculations).
### Subsequent events and cutoff

- November 4, 2026: announced intention to separate into two independent publicly traded companies, intended to be tax-free; expected completion in the first half of 2028, subject to conditions including final Board approval, an effective Form 10 and a tax-free confirmation (Q3 10-Q page:40). This is a subsequent event to the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and is disclosed in a document filed on or before the cutoff. The completion date is a labelled future date, not a fact.
- Nothing in the pack is dated after 2026-11-05.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| On filed figures, leverage fell and interest cover rose through 2026, with statements that agree across sources. The EBITDA behind the ratios is our own definition, so the improvement cannot be tested against covenants. | Medium | The company reports no EBITDA and discloses no covenant levels, so ratios are analyst-defined, and part of the 2026 cash build is attributed to timing. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Total debt to adjusted EBITDA fell from 3.78x at FY2025 to 3.06x on LTM Q3 2026, and net debt to adjusted EBITDA from 3.29x to 2.47x. | Both lower debt and higher earnings contributed, but the measure is analyst-defined because the company reports no EBITDA. | Medium |

| Adjusted EBITDA to cash interest rose from 5.71x at FY2025 to 6.51x on LTM Q3 2026. | Interest burden is covered with room on this basis, which excludes lease payments and litigation settlements. | Medium |

| Operating cash flow for nine months 2026 was far above the prior-year period, and management attributes part of the rise to timing of receipts and payments. | The improvement should not be extrapolated into debt-service capacity without testing the working-capital effect. | Medium |

| Consolidated cash at September 30, 2026 was 11,738, of which about 5,900 was held by the parent or nonrestricted subsidiaries; 7,500 of back-up facilities were undrawn. | Parent-level liquidity is smaller than the consolidated cash figure, and letter-of-credit usage on the facilities is not supplied. | Medium |

| An opioid settlement accrual of about 3,400 and the Omnicare guarantee sit outside the debt figure, and a separation was announced on November 4, 2026. | These claims compete for cash and may reshape the debt and guarantor structure; payment timing and allocation terms are not supplied. | Medium |
### Financial base view

The financial base is usable and shows improving credit metrics, with limits that the committee should hold alongside the ratios. On adjusted EBITDA built as adjusted operating income plus depreciation and amortization less amortization of intangibles, total debt to EBITDA is 3.78x at FY2025 and 3.06x on LTM Q3 2026, net debt to EBITDA 3.29x and 2.47x, and EBITDA to cash interest 5.71x and 6.51x. Both parts of the leverage move contributed: total debt carrying value fell from 64,570 to 60,680 while LTM adjusted EBITDA rose from 17,073 to 19,837. The LTM window now excludes the large 2025 add-backs, so reported and adjusted EBITDA are close on LTM Q3 2026 (19,581 against 19,837), whereas at FY2025 they differ by 7,807, mainly a non-cash goodwill impairment of 5,725. The company reports no EBITDA and the filings disclose no covenant definition or level, so every ratio here is an analyst construct and headroom is Not calculable. Cash is flattered as a deleveraging input: consolidated cash of 11,738 includes cash held outside the parent, and net debt on the parent and nonrestricted cash of about 5,900 gives 2.76x rather than 2.47x. Cash flow from operations for nine months 2026 was 15,318 against 7,249 a year earlier, with the Q3 10-Q attributing the increase to timing of receipts and payments and improved Health Care Benefits performance, so the LTM free cash flow of 15,567 is not a steady-state run rate. Claims outside the debt figure include an opioid settlement accrual of about 3,400, operating lease liabilities of 14,617, the Omnicare guarantee charge of 193 and an announced separation whose financing terms are not supplied.

### EBITDA definitions and add-back review

- No source reports EBITDA or a covenant EBITDA; a search of all seven sources for EBITDA found no hit. Both EBITDA measures here are analyst constructs. The company's own measure is adjusted operating income, which is defined as GAAP operating income excluding amortization of intangible assets, net realized capital gains or losses and other items that neither relate to the ordinary course of business nor reflect underlying performance (Q3 10-Q page:35).

- Reported EBITDA is GAAP operating income plus depreciation and amortization from the cash flow statement. It carries every one-off through the period. In FY2025 it is depressed by the goodwill impairment of 5,725 recorded in Q3 2025.

- Adjusted EBITDA is adjusted operating income plus depreciation and amortization less amortization of intangible assets, because adjusted operating income already adds back that amortization and adding the whole of D&A would count it twice. The check is that adjusted EBITDA less reported EBITDA equals the add-backs other than amortization of intangibles: 7,807 for FY2025 and 256 for LTM Q3 2026.

- FY2025 add-backs other than amortization (10-K page:138): net realized capital losses 44, acquisition-related integration costs 117, goodwill impairment 5,725, Health Care Delivery clinic closure 83, opioid litigation charge 320, office real estate 10, legacy litigation charges 1,220 and loss on Accountable Care assets 288. The litigation items are cash claims, so adjusted EBITDA overstates cash earnings available for debt service in the periods they are paid.
- LTM Q3 2026 add-backs other than amortization of 256 comprise the Omnicare guarantee of 193 and 63 of realized capital losses and integration costs; the 2025 items have rolled out of the window.

- Net investment income of 2,456 on an LTM basis (FY2025 2,233 plus nine months 2026 1,862 less nine months 2025 1,639) is part of revenue and operating income, so EBITDA includes insurance investment income.

- Departures from a covenant definition cannot be assessed because none is disclosed. The only covenant statements are that the facilities and unsecured senior notes contain customary restrictive financial and operating covenants, that they do not accelerate on a downgrade, and that the Company was in compliance at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:64).
### Segment drivers
| Adjusted operating income | FY2025 | Nine months 2025 | Nine months 2026 | Q3 2025 | Q3 2026 |
| Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness | 6,040 | 4,129 | 4,307 | 1,478 | 1,635 |

Health Care Benefits drives the change: its adjusted operating income was 6,379 for nine months 2026 against 3,615, and the medical benefit ratio was 91.3 percent in Q3 2026 against 92.8 percent and 87.8 percent against 90.0 percent for nine months (Q3 release page:2), which the Q3 10-Q (page:54) attributes to improved underlying performance in the Government business. Health Services rose by 100 and Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness by 178 over the nine months, while Corporate/Other was 387 worse. Implied Q4 2025 adjusted operating income for Health Care Benefits is a loss of 676 (2,939 less 3,615), so the LTM window replaces that weak quarter and part of the LTM improvement over FY2025 is a base effect. Underwriting results in one segment are therefore the swing factor for the EBITDA denominator.
### Cash flow quality

- Nine months 2026 operating cash flow was 15,318 against 7,249. The Q3 10-Q (page:63) says the increase was primarily due to the timing of receipts and payments and improved operating performance in Health Care Benefits. Accounts receivable used 2,254 against 7,537 a year earlier and other liabilities provided 2,810 (page:4), so working capital swung. Full-year 2026 guidance is cash flow from operations of at least 15.5 billion (Q3 release page:1).

- LTM operating cash flow of 18,708 is below LTM adjusted EBITDA of 19,837; LTM free cash flow of 15,567 less dividends of 3,423 leaves 12,144. In nine months 2026 the Company repaid 4,057 of long-term debt, issued none, and cash rose from 8,453 to 11,738. No share repurchases appear in the nine months 2026 or 2025 cash flow statements.
- LTM interest paid has stayed between 2,991 and 3,070 across the four dates, so the cover improvement comes from the numerator, not from lower interest.
### Liquidity by facility

- Three unsecured five-year back-up revolving credit facilities of 2,500 each (7,500 in total), all undrawn at September 30, 2026, with no commercial paper outstanding; expiries May 2029, 2030 and 2031; weighted average quarterly facility fee about 0.03 percent (Q3 10-Q page:64). None expires within twelve months.

- Letters of credit drawn on the facilities: Not supplied. Searches for letter of credit, standby, LC and LCs across the 10-K and the Q3 10-Q found nothing, so net availability equals the face amount only on the assumption of no usage, which the sources neither confirm nor deny.

- Consolidated liquidity is 11,738 plus 7,500, which is 19,238. Parent and nonrestricted liquidity is about 5,900 plus 7,500, which is 13,400, because the rest of the cash sits in regulated or restricted subsidiaries. Restricted cash of 210 (in other assets) is excluded. FHLBB advances of up to about 1,400 are available to a subsidiary but are not committed facilities and are excluded.

- Near-term uses: current portion of long-term debt of 3,457, and the current portion of opioid settlement obligations, which was 648 at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:155); the 2026 equivalent is Not supplied.

- Between the March and June 2026 10-Qs the facility expiries moved from May 2028, 2029, 2030 to May 2029, 2030, 2031, with no amendment document in the pack. The later dates are used and labelled as filing wording.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| CVS is a listed, sponsor-free health care group whose credit story is insurance underwriting recovery inside a large pharmacy and benefits platform, with an announced separation that leaves debt allocation and guarantor structure unknown. | Medium | Ownership, board and control rights are not in the pack, and the separation announcement carries no financing, debt allocation or guarantee terms. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Health Care Benefits drove the earnings improvement in 2026, helped by a lower medical benefit ratio, after the individual exchange exit and 2025 reserve deficiencies. | Group earnings depend heavily on underwriting results in one segment, so a reversal in medical costs would feed straight into leverage. | Medium |

| About one fifth of consolidated revenue comes from the federal government, mostly through Medicare contracts. | Government payment policy and annual contract terms are a concentrated source of earnings and cash flow risk. | High |

| A separation into two public companies was announced on November 4, 2026, with completion expected in the first half of 2028. | Existing creditors do not know which company will carry each debt series or whether guarantees will be added; the sources are silent. | Medium |

| The parent recorded a contingent guarantee liability for Omnicare after that subsidiary's Chapter 11 filing in 2025. | The parent has shown it can absorb subsidiary claims, which is a cash call outside the debt figure; terms are not supplied. | Medium |

| No debt was issued in nine months 2026, and the company has paid a steady dividend while making no share repurchases in that period. | Free cash flow in 2026 is going to debt repayment and cash build rather than distributions beyond the dividend. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

CVS Health is a diversified, listed health care company with four reportable segments: Health Care Benefits (the Aetna insurer), Health Services (the CVS Caremark pharmacy benefit manager plus clinical and care delivery businesses including Signify Health and Oak Street Health), Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness (the retail and infusion pharmacy business) and Corporate/Other. For a creditor the mechanics are: a very large, low-margin revenue base dominated by drug pass-through; an insurance segment whose results swing on the medical benefit ratio and on government rate and risk-adjustment policy; a pharmacy segment under reimbursement and price pressure; and a group that carries a large debt stack with unsecured senior notes and two junior subordinated series. The recent history that matters is a reset in 2025 (a goodwill impairment in the care delivery business, exits from accountable care programs, an individual exchange premium deficiency and the Omnicare bankruptcy) followed by a stronger 2026 in which Health Care Benefits recovered and the group repaid debt while leaving the dividend unchanged. The leading uncertainty is the announced separation: it is a proposed transaction, not a completed one, and nothing in the pack says how existing notes, facilities, guarantees or the junior subordinated notes would be allocated. There is no sponsor, no leveraged buyout and no sponsor behaviour to assess, so the governance review rests on documented issuer actions only, and ownership and control detail is Insufficient Information because the proxy statement is incorporated by reference and not supplied.
### Company and operating model
| Item | Fact | Category | Source |

| Business description | A health solutions company with approximately 9,000 retail locations, more than 1,000 walk-in and primary care medical clinics, a pharmacy benefits manager with approximately 87 million plan members and an insurer serving an estimated more than 37 million people (December 31, 2025) | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:5 |
| Reportable segments | Health Care Benefits, Health Services, Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness, Corporate/Other | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:5; Q3 10-Q page:35 |

| Health Care Benefits | Aetna: commercial, Medicare Advantage, Medicare Supplement, Medicare PDP and Medicaid products, both Insured (the Company bears the risk) and ASC (plan sponsor bears the risk) | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:6 to page:7 |

### Company profile

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The only announced transaction is a proposed separation of CVS Health into two independent, publicly traded companies, announced on November 4, 2026 and disclosed as a subsequent event to the September 30, 2026 financial statements (Q3 10-Q page:40 and page:44). It is intended to be tax-free to the Company and its shareholders for U.S. federal income tax purposes. One company would hold Aetna, CVS Caremark, CVS Specialty, Oak Street Health and Signify Health and would carry the CVS Health name in the interim; the other would hold retail pharmacy, mail pharmacy, MinuteClinic including virtual care and the Health100 technology services business and would be named CVS Pharmacy. Completion is expected in the first half of 2028, subject to customary conditions including final approval by the Board, effectiveness of a Form 10 registration statement and a customary confirmation of tax-free treatment. This is a labelled future date, not a fact. The pack gives no purchase price, use of proceeds, new debt, debt allocation, guarantee, change-of-control or covenant treatment for the separation, so its liquidity and leverage effect is Insufficient Information. The creditor mechanic is that two entities will replace one obligor and the existing indentures and facilities will have to be dealt with; whether that is by assumption, guarantee, exchange or retained parent obligations is unknown, and that is the main monitoring item.

On new debt issues, no debt was issued in nine months 2026 (the cash flow statement shows no proceeds from long-term debt and repayments of long-term debt, Q3 10-Q page:4). Earlier issuance in the notes: on May 9, 2024 senior notes of about 5.0 billion dollars in five series for general corporate purposes; on December 10, 2024 two junior subordinated series of 2.25 billion and 750 million dollars with fixed-to-fixed rate resets, whose proceeds funded a cash tender in which about 2.6 billion dollars of senior notes were bought for about 2.0 billion dollars in cash with a gain on early extinguishment of 491 million dollars; and on August 15, 2025 senior notes in four series of 750 million, 1.5 billion, 1.25 billion and 500 million dollars due 2032, 2035, 2055 and 2065 with total proceeds of about 4.0 billion dollars used to repay existing indebtedness including commercial paper and for general corporate purposes (10-K page:151 to page:152). The creditor reading is that the Company has used long-dated issuance and a liability management tender to extend and reshape the stack, and has since moved to repayment. Other transactions relevant to credit are the Omnicare matters and the Rite Aid asset acquisitions below.

### Governance and capital allocation behaviour
Assessment is of issuer-level documented actions only; no individuals are assessed and no behaviour is inferred from ownership because there is no sponsor.
| Behaviour | Evidence | Category | Dimension | Mechanic and implication |

| Debt reduction in 2026 | No issuance and repayments of long-term debt in nine months 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:4) | Analyst Interpretation | Financial policy | Supportive of deleveraging: cash flow is being used to cut debt, though the amount repaid roughly matches scheduled 2026 maturities, so it is not evidence of discretionary prepayment |

| Dividend maintained, no repurchases | Dividend of 0.665 dollars per quarter in both years; no repurchase line (Q3 10-Q page:21, page:4) | Analyst Interpretation | Capital allocation | Distributions are limited to the ordinary dividend, which protects cash for debt service; the repurchase authorizations remain available and could be used |

| Support of a distressed subsidiary | Contingent guarantee liability for Omnicare recorded after the bankruptcy court approved agreements (Q3 10-Q page:39) | Analyst Interpretation | Creditor treatment | The parent is funding claims of a deconsolidated subsidiary rather than leaving them with it; this shows willingness to settle but is a cash call outside the debt figure. Legal capacity and the guarantee terms are not supplied |

| Liability management in 2024 | Tender of about 2.6 billion dollars of senior notes with new junior subordinated issuance (10-K page:152) | Analyst Interpretation | Creditor treatment | A voluntary tender at a discount is a market-based exchange, not a priming or non-pro-rata transaction; the sources show no drop-down, uptier or collateral release |

| Portfolio pruning | Exit from ACO REACH and MSSP, a Health Care Delivery goodwill impairment and the individual exchange exit (Q3 10-Q page:13, page:45; 10-K page:7) | Analyst Interpretation | Strategic discipline | Shows willingness to exit loss-making lines, which supports margin recovery but also shows that acquired care delivery assets (Signify Health, Oak Street Health) have underperformed the price paid |

| Transparency and reporting | Quarterly filings with segment reconciliations, covenant compliance statement and dated subsequent events | Analyst Interpretation | Disclosure | Reporting is regular and consistent, but covenant levels, guarantor detail and indenture terms are not disclosed in the pack |

| Separation | Announced intention to separate into two companies (Q3 10-Q page:40) | Documentary Fact | Strategic change | Potentially changes obligor, guarantor and diversification profile; no creditor protections or debt allocation are described. Willingness is untested until terms are published |
### Credit translations

1. Revenue durability. Evidence: Health Care Benefits revenue from the federal government is approximately 20 percent of consolidated revenues, and Medicare contracts with CMS are the large majority of it (10-K page:11); Medicare Advantage membership was 4,229 thousand at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:55). Mechanic: government contracts are annual and subject to rate notices and risk adjustment, so revenue is visible but earnings depend on policy. Implication: revenue durability is good but margin resilience depends on government rates and medical cost trend, so leverage tolerance should be tested for a reversal in the Government business medical benefit ratio. No logged conflict counters this.

2. Margin and cash flow risk. Evidence: the medical benefit ratio was 87.8 percent for nine months 2026 against 90.0 percent, with lower favorable prior period development (Q3 10-Q page:55), and Health Care Benefits adjusted operating income rose strongly (financial base handoff). Mechanic: small changes in the ratio on a premium base of this size move group earnings. Implication: the improvement in leverage reported in the financial base handoff rests on one segment and is not yet a through-the-cycle measure; monitoring should centre on medical cost trend and prior period development.

3. Concentration risk. Evidence: no single Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness payor is 10 percent or more of revenue (10-K page:29), while Health Services revenue growth is driven by drug mix and brand inflation with client price improvements (Q3 10-Q page:58). Mechanic: PBM contracts reprice at renewal and legislation targets PBM activities (Q3 10-Q page:48). Implication: the largest client terms are not disclosed, so concentration inside the PBM cannot be judged.

4. Sponsor alignment. There is no sponsor; ownership alignment cannot be assessed beyond the dividend and repurchase record. Implication: no sponsor extraction or support risk applies; public shareholder distributions are modest and documented.

5. Key uncertainties. Evidence: separation announced for completion in the first half of 2028 (Q3 10-Q page:40); opioid accrual of about 3.4 billion dollars remaining (Q3 10-Q page:28); Omnicare guarantee (page:39). Mechanic: each is a claim or a structural change that the debt figure does not capture. Implication: refinancing and guarantor analysis should wait for the Form 10 and any indenture amendments; the committee should not assume that existing creditors keep their current obligor.
### Conflicts logged

None found. The back-up facility expiry wording differs between the Q1 and Q2 10-Qs (May 2028, 2029 and 2030 against May 2029, 2030 and 2031); this is a change over time and is recorded as a version difference, not reconciled. The financial base handoff's correction of the note-line count (47 with a balance, not 49) is carried here.
### Consumers
| Module | Readiness | What it should take | Why it matters | Gap and required action |

| CP-2 | Ready with limitations | Segment drivers, government concentration, separation as an open event, governance table and credit translations | The synthesis needs business risk and structural change alongside the leverage and liquidity figures | Ownership and control detail, PBM client terms and separation financing are Insufficient Information; carry them as open items and avoid a pro forma structure |

| CP-5 | Ready with limitations | Every fact row with its category and locator, and the conflicts log | The evidence trace needs each claim tied to a quote or figure and an explicit category | Management Language rows (release claims) must not be traced as filing facts; the stale non-affiliate market value is dated June 30, 2025 |
## Calculations

No new calculations were made in this handoff. Figures are taken as printed or from the financial base handoff, and no derived ratio is introduced. The only arithmetic implied by the text is a comparison of printed values: commercial Insured membership of 3,447 thousand at December 31, 2025 against 2,565 thousand at September 30, 2026, and total medical membership of 26,591 thousand against 26,120 thousand, each from the same table (Q3 10-Q page:55). Not calculable: the effect of the separation on leverage, because no allocation is supplied.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Remediation |

| Ownership, large holders, control rights, board composition and executive arrangements are not in the pack (10-K Part III incorporated by reference to a proxy statement not supplied). | Medium | Obtain the 2026 proxy statement; until then ownership is Insufficient Information. |

| Separation terms: debt allocation, guarantees, change-of-control and covenant treatment, financing and ratings treatment are not supplied. | High | Monitor the Form 10 and any indenture or facility amendments; treat as an open event. |

| Omnicare agreements and the amount and timing of any cash settlement behind the contingent guarantee liability are not supplied. | Medium | Obtain the bankruptcy court documents; treat as a contingent claim outside debt. |
| PBM client concentration, contract terms and rebate pass-through are not disclosed. | Medium | Search the 10-K risk factors in a later pass or obtain client disclosures. |

| Legal capacity under the indentures and facilities (restricted payments, liens, guarantees, subsidiary debt) cannot be assessed because the debt documents are not in the pack. | Medium | Obtain indentures and credit agreements. |
| Covenant levels, guarantor lists and letters of credit remain Not supplied, as in the financial base handoff. | High | Obtain the facility agreement and indentures. |
| Management claims in releases (star ratings, AI deployment, guidance) are not verified by filings. | Low | Cite only as Management Language. |
## Next module

CP-2, the fundamental credit synthesis. It should open the financial base handoff for leverage, interest cover, liquidity, maturities and claims, and this handoff for business drivers, government concentration, governance behaviour, the separation and the credit translations. Carry forward: underwriting results in Health Care Benefits drive the earnings improvement; ownership and control, PBM client terms, separation financing, guarantor detail and covenant levels are not supplied; the opioid accrual, Omnicare guarantee and separation sit outside the debt figure; and no recovery or peer conclusion is made at this stage.

Fundamental credit synthesis for CVS HEALTH Corp (issuer id cvs, registrant CVS Health Corporation), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot. It combines the financial base [CP-1] and the business and transaction context [CP-1A] into a credit view, key findings, strengths, weaknesses and risks, in USD with Q3 2026 as the current period and FY2025 as the prior period. It gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on

The figures are taken from the two upstream handoffs; the source files were reopened only to confirm the figures used below (the debt table, liquidity, ratings, segment tables and the separation note) and to search again for covenant terms, letters of credit and guarantor detail.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| CVS is an improving, moderate-leverage credit with solid liquidity, but its 2026 progress depends on one insurance segment and on a separation whose debt, guarantee and covenant treatment is unknown. | Medium | Covenant levels, guarantor terms, letters of credit and separation financing are not supplied, and the leverage ratios use our own EBITDA definition. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Total debt to adjusted EBITDA fell from 3.78x at FY2025 to 3.06x on LTM Q3 2026, and cash interest cover rose to 6.51x. | Debt service capacity improved on reported figures through both lower debt and higher earnings. | Medium |

| Health Care Benefits supplied more than the whole net rise in adjusted operating income over FY2025. | Group leverage is exposed to one segment's medical benefit ratio and government policy. | Medium |

| Cash was USD 11,738 million, of which about USD 5,900 million was held by the parent or nonrestricted subsidiaries, and USD 7,500 million of facilities were undrawn. | Parent-level liquidity covers near-term debt, dividends and the opioid payment with room, but not without the facilities. | Medium |

| The announced separation, the opioid accrual and the Omnicare guarantee are claims or changes outside the debt figure. | They can pull cash or change the obligor, and their terms are not disclosed. | Medium |
### Credit view

CVS Health Corporation is an improving, moderate-leverage credit whose 2026 progress rests heavily on one segment. The strongest support is deleveraging: total debt to adjusted EBITDA fell to 3.06x on LTM Q3 2026 from 3.78x at FY2025, adjusted EBITDA to cash interest rose to 6.51x, and undrawn back-up facilities of USD 7,500 million sit beside cash of USD 11,738 million. The weakest point is that Health Care Benefits supplied more than the whole net rise in adjusted operating income, while covenant levels, guarantor terms and the debt allocation under the announced separation are not disclosed. What decides the outcome is whether the medical benefit ratio holds, and what the separation does to the obligor and guarantee structure before completion, expected in the first half of 2028.
### Key findings

First, leverage and cover have improved on both numerator and denominator. Total debt carrying value fell from USD 64,570 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 60,680 million at September 30, 2026 while LTM adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 17,073 million to USD 19,837 million, taking total debt to adjusted EBITDA from 3.78x to 3.06x and net debt to adjusted EBITDA from 3.29x to 2.47x [CP-1]. The mechanic is repayment of USD 4,057 million of long-term debt with no issuance in nine months 2026 and higher earnings, so debt service is better covered. The implication is lower refinancing and leverage risk, but the EBITDA is our construct because the company reports none and discloses no covenant definition.

Second, the earnings recovery is concentrated. Adjusted operating income by segment moved from USD 14,443 million at FY2025 to USD 17,098 million on LTM Q3 2026; Health Care Benefits rose by USD 2,764 million while Health Services rose by USD 100 million, Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness by USD 178 million and Corporate/Other fell by USD 387 million (Calculations). Health Care Benefits recorded an implied loss of USD 676 million in Q4 2025 [CP-1], so the LTM window replaces a weak quarter, and its medical benefit ratio of 87.8 percent for nine months 2026 against 90.0 percent reflects the absence of 2025 premium deficiency reserves and lower favorable prior period development [CP-1A]. The mechanic is underwriting leverage on a large premium base; the implication is that a reversal would raise leverage quickly (see the sensitivity below).

Third, liquidity is adequate but less deep than the consolidated cash suggests. Consolidated cash of USD 11,738 million includes about USD 5,900 million held by the parent or nonrestricted subsidiaries, plus USD 7,500 million of undrawn facilities that now expire in May 2029, 2030 and 2031, and no commercial paper [CP-1]. Against that, the next twelve months include a current portion of long-term debt of USD 3,457 million, a dividend of about USD 3,423 million on an LTM basis and an opioid settlement obligation whose current portion was USD 648 million at December 31, 2025, together USD 7,528 million; parent-level liquidity of USD 13,400 million covers that 1.78x. The weak spots are that letters of credit on the facilities are not supplied and that nine months 2026 operating cash flow of USD 15,318 million was helped by working-capital timing.

Fourth, claims outside the debt figure and a structural change sit over the credit. The opioid accrual was about USD 3.4 billion at September 30, 2026, operating lease liabilities were USD 14,617 million, the Omnicare guarantee charge was USD 193 million, and the separation announced on November 4, 2026 would create two companies [CP-1, CP-1A]. The mechanic is competing calls on cash and a possible change of obligor or guarantors; the implication is that leverage on the debt figure alone understates claims, and the amendment, assumption or guarantee route for the notes is the main monitoring item.

Fifth, the information that would let a committee set protections is missing. Covenant levels and headroom, issuer and guarantor by series, indenture terms and letters of credit are not supplied, and ownership detail is not in the pack [CP-0, CP-1, CP-1A]. The ratings (BBB at Fitch with a Negative outlook, Baa3 at Moody's with a Positive outlook, BBB at S&P with a Stable outlook, company statements) are described by the company as investment grade, and one agency holds a Negative outlook. The implication is that the view is a fundamental one and the protection analysis is unfinished.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. The group has scale and diversification across insurance, pharmacy benefits and retail pharmacy, with USD 420,614 million of LTM revenue and adjusted operating income positive in three of four segments [CP-1]. Deleveraging has been funded from internal cash flow, with USD 12,144 million of LTM free cash flow after dividends, no 2026 issuance and no share repurchases in nine months 2026 [CP-1, CP-1A]. Liquidity is supported by USD 7,500 million of undrawn facilities with the earliest expiry in May 2029, so no facility matures within twelve months [CP-1]. The maturity profile is manageable in the near term, with USD 3,379 million due in 2027 and USD 5,008 million in 2028 per the schedule at December 31, 2025, against LTM free cash flow of USD 15,567 million and the facilities [CP-1]. Reporting is regular and discloses segment reconciliations and subsequent events [CP-1A].

Weaknesses. Earnings are concentrated: Health Care Benefits drove the improvement and about 20 percent of consolidated revenue comes from the federal government, mainly Medicare contracts [CP-1A]. Protections cannot be assessed because covenant levels, guarantors and indentures are not supplied [CP-0, CP-1]. Cash is partly outside the parent, and letters of credit usage is unknown [CP-1]. The debt stack includes USD 3,000 million of junior subordinated notes in two series and unsecured senior notes, so structural and ranking questions arise on a separation [CP-1]. Claims outside debt are large: the opioid accrual, lease liabilities and the Omnicare guarantee [CP-1, CP-1A]. The separation introduces an unresolved change of obligor, and pharmacy segments face reimbursement and price pressure, with Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness revenue down 2.0 percent in Q3 2026 [CP-1A].
### Credit assessment and thesis
| Item | Content | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Assessment | Improving, moderate-leverage credit with adequate liquidity; earnings recovery concentrated in Health Care Benefits; protection and separation terms undisclosed | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Leverage, cover and liquidity figures in the financial base; segment and separation rows in the business context |

| Thesis | CVS has deleveraged on internal cash flow and rising insurance earnings, so its credit quality turns on holding the medical benefit ratio and on how the separation treats existing creditors | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | As above |

| Confidence limits | Below High because the readiness and business context handoffs list unresolved High gaps (covenants, guarantors, separation terms) | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Gaps in the financial base and business context |
### Basis register for strengths and weaknesses
| Label | Text | Category | Basis |
| Strength: deleveraging | Total debt to adjusted EBITDA 3.78x to 3.06x; net 3.29x to 2.47x | Documentary Fact | Leverage chart data in the financial base |
| Strength: interest cover | Adjusted EBITDA to cash interest 5.71x to 6.51x | Documentary Fact | Interest cover chart data |
| Strength: liquidity | Cash USD 11,738 million, undrawn facilities USD 7,500 million, none expiring within twelve months | Documentary Fact | Liquidity chart data and facility review |

| Strength: capital allocation | Debt repayment, no issuance, ordinary dividend, no repurchases in nine months 2026 | Analyst Interpretation | Cash flow rows and governance table in the business context |

| Weakness: concentration | Health Care Benefits supplies more than the whole net improvement; federal government about 20 percent of revenue | Analyst Interpretation | Segment drivers and customer concentration rows |

| Weakness: protections unknown | Covenant levels, guarantors, indentures and letters of credit not supplied | Insufficient Information | Gaps in all upstream handoffs; the missing data matter because headroom and ranking cannot be assessed |

| Weakness: outside-debt claims | Opioid accrual about USD 3.4 billion, operating leases USD 14,617 million, Omnicare guarantee USD 193 million | Documentary Fact | Claims table in the financial base |
| Weakness: separation | Terms, debt allocation and guarantees not disclosed | Insufficient Information | Transaction summary in the business context |
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Insurance underwriting reversal | A higher medical benefit ratio on the Government and other books lowers Health Care Benefits adjusted operating income, which supplied the net improvement | Leverage rises quickly; with Health Care Benefits at zero for twelve months, total debt to adjusted EBITDA would be 4.29x (Calculations) | Material |

| Separation and obligor change | Two companies replace one; existing notes and facilities need assumption, exchange or guarantees | Unknown allocation of USD 60,680 million of debt and the junior subordinated notes; refinancing and ranking risk | Material |
| Undisclosed covenants and guarantors | Only a compliance statement exists | Headroom and structural ranking cannot be assessed | Material |

| Contingent and litigation claims | Opioid settlement payments, the Omnicare guarantee and derivative litigation draw on cash | Reduces cash available for debt service outside the debt figure | Material |

| Cash flow quality | Nine months 2026 operating cash flow was lifted by timing of receipts and payments | LTM free cash flow of USD 15,567 million may overstate sustainable debt service capacity | Material |
| Government payment concentration | About 20 percent of revenue is from the federal government, mostly Medicare | Rate notices, risk adjustment and policy changes affect earnings | Material |

| Pharmacy margin pressure | Reimbursement pressure, price reductions and generic introductions in Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness; PBM legislation | Slower growth in two segments that provide stable cash flow | Minor |
| Cash held outside the parent | About USD 5,900 million of USD 11,738 million is parent or nonrestricted | Net leverage on parent cash is 2.76x rather than 2.47x | Minor |
| Maturity wall | USD 5,008 million due in 2028 including the 4.3% senior notes of USD 5,000 million due March 2028 | Refinancing or repayment from cash flow; well within LTM free cash flow | Minor |
### Consistency with upstream handoffs

This synthesis is consistent with the readiness, financial base and business context handoffs. The 47-of-49 note-line correction in the financial base is carried unchanged.

Inputs are from the financial base handoff unless stated; amounts in USD millions.
| Calculation | Formula and result |

| LTM adjusted operating income by segment | FY2025 plus nine months 2026 less nine months 2025: Health Care Benefits 2,939 + 6,379 - 3,615 = 5,703; Health Services 7,151 + 5,328 - 5,228 = 7,251; Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness 6,040 + 4,307 - 4,129 = 6,218; Corporate/Other (1,687) + (1,513) - (1,126) = (2,074); total 5,703 + 7,251 + 6,218 - 2,074 = 17,098, equal to the financial base |

| Change against FY2025 | Health Care Benefits 5,703 - 2,939 = 2,764; Health Services 7,251 - 7,151 = 100; Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness 6,218 - 6,040 = 178; Corporate/Other (2,074) - (1,687) = (387); net 17,098 - 14,443 = 2,655, equal to 2,764 + 100 + 178 - 387. Health Care Benefits (2,764) exceeds the net change (2,655) |

| Sensitivity: Health Care Benefits back to FY2025 level | LTM adjusted EBITDA 19,837 - 2,764 = 17,073. Total debt / EBITDA 60,680 / 17,073 = 3.55x; net 48,942 / 17,073 = 2.87x; EBITDA / cash interest 17,073 / 3,048 = 5.60x |

| Sensitivity: Health Care Benefits at zero for twelve months (hypothetical, not a forecast) | LTM adjusted EBITDA 19,837 - 5,703 = 14,134. Total debt / EBITDA 60,680 / 14,134 = 4.29x; net 48,942 / 14,134 = 3.46x; EBITDA / cash interest 14,134 / 3,048 = 4.64x |

| Parent-level liquidity cover | About 5,900 + 7,500 = 13,400; 13,400 / 7,528 = 1.78x. The 5,900 is approximate as printed |
